title: Did Lakshmana Never Sleep?
status: DRAFT v1 (part 2 of 2, follows A17) — Ayodhya 2.41, 2.44-45, 2.47, 2.49-50 read; review before posting

shots.hi: क्या लक्ष्मण, वनवास में, सच में कभी नहीं सोए?
shots.en: Did Lakshmana really never sleep in the forest?
units: [serious] क्या लक्ष्मण, वनवास में, सच में कभी नहीं सोए?

shots.hi: वाल्मीकि रामायण, अयोध्या कांड, सर्ग पचास। स सुप्तः समये भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणः प्रतिबोधितः । जहौ निद्रां च तन्द्रीं च प्रसक्तं च पथि श्रमम् ॥ ये है असली कहानी।

sloka.en: “Lakshmana, who had been asleep, was woken at the right time by his brother; he shook off sleep, drowsiness and the weariness of the road.”
sloka.translit: sa suptaḥ samaye bhrātrā lakṣmaṇaḥ pratibodhitaḥ, jahau nidrāṃ ca tandrīṃ ca prasaktaṃ ca pathi śramam

shots.en: The second night, by the Ganga. Guha, king of the Nishadas, says to Lakshmana:

shots.en: "Prince, this bed is for you. Sleep in comfort. We will keep watch all night."

shots.en: "While my brother lies on the bare ground with Sita, how could I sleep? How could I live, or know any comfort?"

avoid: calling the Urmila story 'fake' or mocking it: it is a later, loving telling of her sacrifice
naming or quoting a specific later text for the Nidra legend (none verified)
saying Lakshmana slept 'often' or 'every night': Valmiki shows him awake (2.41, 2.44-45) and asleep once (2.50.1-3)
the Indrajit 'only one who has not slept 14 years' legend: not checked, not claimed
inventing a farewell between Lakshmana and Urmila (none in the CE)

verify_note: Whole CE searched (Bala 76, Ayodhya 111, Aranya 71, Kishkindha 66, Sundara 66, Yuddha 116, Uttara 100 sargas): ऊर्मिला only at 1.70.21-22, 1.71.3, 1.72.18, 1.76.9 and 2.110.51 (1.32.12 is another Urmila, a gandharvi's mother). No Nidra Devi, no 14-year sleep. Nights: 1 Tamasa 2.41.12-14 (Lakshmana awake all night with Sumantra); 2 Shringaverapura 2.44.25-26, 2.45.2-3 (Guha offers the bed), 2.45.9 (Lakshmana's reply); 3 under a tree past the Ganga 2.47.1-3 (Rama: we two must keep awake); 4 Bharadvaja 2.48-49.1; 5 by the Yamuna 2.49.15; morning 2.50.1-3 Rama gently wakes the sleeping Lakshmana. caption: Part 2 of 2. In Valmiki's Ramayana, Lakshmana stays awake all night on the Tamasa, telling Sumantra of Rama's virtues. By the Ganga, Guha offers him a bed, and he answers: "How could I sleep while my brother lies on the bare ground with Sita?" Past the Ganga, Rama says: "From today, we two must keep watch." And by the Yamuna, Valmiki writes that Rama gently woke Lakshmana, who had been sleeping beside him. He kept watch, and he slept too. Both tellings are told with devotion.
